_note: Companions walking out (see src/away.js and docs/STORY-BIBLE.md). In Book Two, a companion whose approval falls by 2 or more over one chapter (counting its side jobs and camp scene) leaves after it for the next chapter ('leave'), and comes back when that chapter is done ('back'). If the next chapter needs them (quests.json 'needs'), they stay and say so instead ('stay'); the flag away:stay-<id> holds that chapter's id for the lines. Every choice here ends at the town the party is in, or, below the stair (chapters 17 to 19 go straight on), at the next chapter's opening. Lines spoken by a companion who is not in the party are skipped, so a line answering one needs a 'when'.

lines.narrate: Orin is waiting by the gate in the morning with his pack on. That is how you know, before he says anything. He has tied it for a long march, with the knot he says is the only one worth using.

oneOf.text: I'm going to walk with the carters on the Highpass road for a while. Everything the Wold's people need has to be carried up or down it, and the council's short of carriers. I'm good at it.
I'm going to walk with the carters on the Highpass road for a while. The council's always short of somebody to load a wagon. I'm good at it.
I'm going to walk with the relief carts for a while. Somebody has to load them. I'm good at it.

lines.text: You've been making choices I'd have argued with. I didn't argue. I stood behind you and held the door, the way I do. That's on me, not you. But I can't keep standing behind things I'd have said no to. That's how I ended up leaving people on a road once.
I'm not leaving. I'm going away to think. It's different. I'll be back when the next thing's done.
Orin Stoneward. Are you sulking?
I'm walking. Sulking's sitting down.
You're going now? Who's going to carry the—
You are. Lift with your knees.
I'll find you. It's not hard. Follow the arguing.

lines.narrate: He goes out through the gate and does not look back. At the bend in the road he stops to re-tie a strap that did not need it. Then he is gone.

lines.text: No. Ask me again after. If you still want to.

lines.narrate: He goes out through the gate and does not look back. At the bend in the road he stops to re-tie a strap that did not need it. Then he is gone.

oneOf.narrate: Orin finds you on the vault floor before you go down, with his pack on. He has tied it for a long march.
Orin finds you at the foot of the ledge while the others sleep, with his pack on. He has tied it for a long march, with a plain knot.
Orin finds you at the edge of the floor of given things while the others sleep, with his pack on, tied with a plain knot.
Orin finds you before breakfast. He has his pack with him, and he has tied it for a long march.

lines.text: I was going to walk for a while. I've been standing behind choices I'd have argued with, and I don't like what that makes me.
But it's Kell's Bridge next. If it's who I think it is on that bridge, I'm the one at the front. So I'm staying. After that, we talk.
But it's the Mother Bell next, and there'll be a door to hold. I don't walk away from doors. After, we talk. If there's an after.
But they're deciding about Elske next, and I'll stand in that hall whatever I think of you this week. After that, we talk.
But it's Saltwick next. Mags sent word: they've caught my old captain, and the roof council's going to try him. If they're trying that night, I'm in the room. After that, we talk.
But it's Vell next, and the stair. Once we're down there, there's no walking back to anyone. I'm not letting you go down a hole I haven't checked first. After, if there's an after, we talk.
But it's down, now. There's no road to walk off on, only the stair, and I'm not letting you go down it with nobody at your back. After, if there's an after, we talk.
But there's nowhere down here to walk to. And I'm not leaving anyone in the dark. Not again. Not even you. After, we talk.
But Hesk's at the heart of that ring, and somebody has to stand next to you when you go in. After, we talk.
But it's Saltwick next, and Davin's packed. Mags wrote. If the boy's going to ask to come north on my word, he asks me to my face, and I answer him to his. After that, we talk.
But it's the peaks next. Nobody walks off a mountain, and I'm not having you on a rope with nobody behind you. After, on the other side, we talk.

oneOf.narrate: He puts the pack down. He does not untie it.
He puts the pack down. He does not untie it.
He unties the march knot and ties an ordinary one. It seems to cost him something.

lines.text: After.

lines.narrate: Orin comes back the way he left: on foot, with his pack, at an hour nobody expected. He is browner than he was, and there is a new graze across his knuckles that he says came from a crate.

oneOf.text: Carried for the Wold's people on the Highpass road for a fortnight. Flour, mostly, and blankets. Nobody asked me what I thought about anything. It was very restful for about three days.
Loaded the council's wagons on the Highpass road for a fortnight. Nobody asked me what I thought about anything. It was very restful for about three days.
Loaded carts for a fortnight. Nobody asked me what I thought about anything. It was very restful for about three days.

lines.text: Then a carter asked me which road was safer. I told him, and he took the other one anyway, and I was angry all afternoon. Not because he was wrong. Because he never asked me why.
So. I'm asking. Why?

choices.label: Tell him why you chose what you did

lines.narrate: You tell him. All of it, the reasons you had and the ones you made up afterwards. He listens the way he listens to a plan: all the way through, without interrupting, looking for the weak joint.

lines.text: I'd still have argued.
But I'd have been arguing with a reason. Not a whim. I can do that. That's most of what I'm for.

choices.label: Tell him he was right, and you were wrong

lines.text: Not all of it.
Some. Enough to walk. Not enough to stay gone.

lines.narrate: He holds out his hand. You shake it. He has a grip like a door being shut, firmly, on a draught.

choices.label: Tell him you'd do it all again

lines.text: I know. That's why I came back.
Somebody has to say the uncomfortable thing when you do. Might as well be someone who can't lie about it.

lines.narrate: Maren finds you after supper, when the others have gone up. She has her shrine-satchel over her shoulder and her list in her hand, and she sits down across the table from you as if for cards.

Maren finds you after supper, when the others have gone up. She has her shrine-satchel over her shoulder, and her hands are empty in a way they never used to be, and she sits down across the table from you as if for cards.

lines.text: I'm going to go and sit with someone who doesn't need anything decided, for a while. There's always a shrine. There's always someone in it who would like company and no advice.

I hear what people mean, you know. Not only what they say. Lately I keep hearing you mean well, and then do things I can't stand beside. I don't think you're lying to me. I think you may be lying to yourself, a little. I can't hear that from this close.
I'll come back. I always come back. I just need to be somewhere quiet enough to hear myself think.
You're going? Who's going to— Maren. Who's going to fuss?
You'll have to do it yourself, Nessa. You'll be appalling at it.
Take the good blanket.
I already have it, Orin. I always have it.
Thank you. That was the right answer.

lines.narrate: She leaves before morning. On the table there is the stew-pot, scoured clean, and a note in her small careful hand: Back soon. Don't use this.

choices.label: Ask her what you should have done

lines.text: That isn't how it works. If I tell you, you'll do it for me, and then I'm back where I started, only worse, because I'll have been right.

lines.narrate: She leaves before morning. On the table there is the stew-pot, scoured clean, and a note in her small careful hand: Back soon. Don't use this.

oneOf.narrate: Maren finds you on the vault floor before you go down, with her satchel packed. She sits down beside you on the cold iron, and after a while she takes the satchel off her shoulder and puts it down.

Maren finds you at the foot of the ledge while the others sleep, with her satchel packed. She sits down beside you on the rock, and after a while she takes the satchel off her shoulder and puts it down.

Maren finds you at the edge of the floor of given things while the others sleep, with her satchel packed. She sits down beside you, and after a while she takes the satchel off her shoulder and puts it down.
Maren finds you after supper with her satchel packed. She sits down across the table from you, and then, after a while, she takes the satchel off her shoulder and puts it on the floor.

lines.text: I was going to go and sit in a shrine somewhere for a while. I keep hearing you mean well and do things I can't stand beside.
But Anwen's note is in my pocket, and I've carried her name for six years. I'm not going anywhere tonight. After the Sallows, we'll talk.
But Elske is riding for the Mother Bell, and somebody who can hear her should be in that hall. After, we'll talk.
But they're deciding what to do with Elske, and I want to hear what she says. And what you say. After that, we'll talk.
But it's Highpass next, and the council's letter is addressed to me. Whatever they want of me, I'll answer it myself, and I'd like you there when I do. After that, we'll talk.
But it's the stair next. Nobody who goes down it can come back for anyone who stayed behind, and I won't be the one you have to leave. After, we'll talk.
But there's no shrine down a stair. There's nowhere to go that isn't with you. So I'll come, and I'll say so when I can't stand beside it. After, we'll talk.
But it takes things down here, and I want somebody near you who'll notice what it takes. After, we'll talk.
But somebody has to hear Hesk, at the end, and hear whether he means it. After, we'll talk.

oneOf.text: But it's Highpass next, and Rue's asked me to sit with her when she reads her book to the council. She's never asked anybody to sit with her. After that, we'll talk.
But Rue's written. She wants me at Highpass. She didn't say why, and she always says why. After that, we'll talk.

lines.text: But it's the crossing. There's no shrine on a mountain, and I want to hear the first thing the Wold says to us. After, we'll talk.
After. I'll hold you to it. I keep lists, you know.

lines.narrate: Maren comes back on a market day, with a basket of eggs somebody gave her and a bandage on her hand that she says she gave to somebody else first.

oneOf.text: I sat in a shrine and listened to people. Nobody asked me to fix anything. A door-bearer from the Wold told me about her street for an hour, every door in it, in order, and every word was true. It was the most restful hour of my life.

I sat in a shrine and listened to people. Nobody asked me to fix anything. A carter's wife told me about the north road for an hour, what it was like before the white came down it, and none of it was true, and she meant every word. It was the most restful hour of my life.
I sat in a shrine and listened to people. Nobody asked me to fix anything. A woman told me about her husband's feet for an hour. It was the most restful hour of my life.

lines.text: I've decided I'm not your conscience. I'm your friend. They aren't the same thing, and I'd been doing the wrong one.
So, as your friend. Don't tell me why. Tell me how it felt.

choices.label: Tell her honestly how it felt

lines.narrate: It takes longer than you expect. She does not interrupt once.

lines.text: Thank you. You meant all of that. I could hear it. That's enough to go on with.
That isn't true.
But you'd like it to be, and I can work with that. I've worked with worse. I've worked with Orin.
I know. I could hear it from the door.

lines.narrate: She puts the eggs on the table and takes the stew-pot down from the shelf, and nobody, for once, says a word against it.
Nessa does not say goodbye. In the morning her bedroll is gone, and so is Biscuit, and there is a letter on your pack in her handwriting, which runs uphill.
It is finished. That is how you know she means it.

oneOf.narrate: 'Gone out on the roads for a bit. Don't come after me, I'm faster than you. You keep making people wait. I know you've got reasons. You've always got reasons. But the Wold's waited nine hundred years, and it's still waiting, at our own gate now, and I can't keep watching you make it wait while you think. I need to be somewhere for a while where if someone needs help I can just go. Back after the next thing. Took Biscuit. He agreed. N.'

'Gone out on the roads for a bit. Don't come after me, I'm faster than you. You keep making people wait. I know you've got reasons. You've always got reasons. But there's a whole country up north that's been waiting nine hundred years, and I can't keep watching you make people wait down here first. I need to be somewhere for a while where if someone needs help I can just go. Back after the next thing. Took Biscuit. He agreed. N.'

'Gone out on the roads for a bit. Don't come after me, I'm faster than you. You keep making people wait. I know you've got reasons. You've always got reasons. But I've been the one hanging upside down in a snare while people talked about the best way to cut me down, and I'm not doing that to anybody else. I need to be somewhere for a while where if someone needs help I can just go. Back after the next thing. Took Biscuit. He agreed. N.'

lines.narrate: 'P.S. This one I'm leaving where you'll find it. So you know.'

lines.text: She finished one.
She'll be back. She left the good rope.

choices.label: Fold the letter and keep it

lines.narrate: You fold it along the creases she made and put it somewhere safe. It is the first letter Nessa Reed has ever finished and left where somebody would read it.
The road is empty for a mile in both directions. Whoever taught Nessa to leave without being seen did a very good job of it. You stand there long enough to feel foolish, and then a little longer.

oneOf.narrate: Nessa is sitting at the rim of the iron door with a letter in her lap that she has, for once, finished.
Nessa is sitting on the ledge with a letter in her lap that she has, for once, finished. She has to hold it close to the lamp to see it.
Nessa is sitting at the edge of the floor of given things with a letter in her lap that she has, for once, finished.
Nessa is sitting on the step with a letter in her lap that she has, for once, finished.

lines.text: I was going to go. Out on the roads for a bit. You keep making people wait, and I keep being the one who— never mind. I wrote it down. It's a very good letter.
But Wren's at Cinder Fold. Wren. So I'm not going anywhere except there.
But it's the Mother Bell. Everyone's going to be there. I'm not missing that to sulk on a road.
But they're deciding about Elske, and I want to see your face when you answer her.
But Wren's written. From Cinder Fold. The committee's voted, and she's said yes, and I'm not going anywhere except there.
But it's the stair. Under Vell. You're not going down a hole in the ground without someone who can find the way back, and that's me. That's always been me.
But it's the stair. You're not going down a hole in the ground without someone who can find the way back, and that's me.
But there's nowhere to go down here. I looked. I'm good at looking. It's all down.
But it's the last bit. I'm not missing the last bit.
But it's Cinder Fold next. Wren's there, and the key, and Hew. I'm not going anywhere except there.
But it's Cinder Fold next. The tenth bell's there, and the key, and Hew. I'm not going anywhere except there.
But it's the peaks. Over the top and down into the Wold, where nobody's been for nine hundred years. Somebody's got to go first. That's me.

lines.narrate: She folds the letter and puts it in her pocket. The one for later.

lines.text: Later. Don't read it. I'll know.

lines.narrate: Nessa comes back over a wall rather than through a gate, because that is how she does everything, with Biscuit behind her and a fresh scratch on her cheek and a great deal to say.

oneOf.text: I found a carter in a ditch on the Highpass road. And a door-bearer from Lantry who'd never seen a tree, so I showed her eleven. And two kids from Cinder Fold who'd set off up the Highpass road to see the Wold for themselves. And I took them all back, not in that order. Nobody made me wait for anything. It was brilliant.

I found a carter in a ditch on the Highpass road. And a lost goat. And two kids from Cinder Fold who'd set off up the Highpass road to look for the north. And I took them all back, not in that order. Nobody made me wait for anything. It was brilliant.

I found a carter in a ditch. And a lost goat, not Brannagh's, a different goat. And two kids who'd run off from a farm. And I took them all back, not in that order. Nobody made me wait for anything. It was brilliant.

lines.text: And then I kept turning round to tell someone about it, and there wasn't anyone. Which was stupid. So.
Did you read my letter? Don't answer that.

choices.label: “I read it. You were right about some of it.”

lines.text: Some of it. I'll take some. Some's loads.

choices.label: Ask Biscuit how he got on

oneOf.text: He says it was very boring without you, and the door-bearer from Lantry wrote his name on her arm, and he would like a crust.
He says it was very boring without you, and the goat was rude to him, and he would like a crust.

lines.narrate: Biscuit, consulted, does not disagree.

lines.text: Ha. Good one. No.
...Maybe. If you're quick.
